spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Multiplying the critical-line zeta value by a phase produces a real smooth Hardy function without changing its modulus or critical-line zero set. This turns complex zero geometry into real zero-endpoint intervals, while paired moments of Z and Z' compress amplitude and variation into quantities that endpoint inequalities can compare.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines Z(t) as a phase multiple of ζ(1/2+it), states that Z is real and smooth for real t, that |Z(t)|=|ζ(1/2+it)|, and that its zeros correspond to critical-line zeta zeros. It then defines I_k(T)=∫|Z|^{2k} and M_k(T)=∫|Z'|^{2k} and records conjectural asymptotic families with different logarithmic powers.
directed.conceptual_reading: The phase adjustment is a representation change that preserves the modulus and relevant zero locus while exposing real-variable differentiability. The two moment families are global summaries of size and variation; their separation makes a function-versus-derivative comparison available without retaining pointwise behavior.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Hardy's phase factor bridges ζ on the critical line to a real function. Zero correspondence then supplies real intervals with zero endpoints, and the I_k/M_k pair is the bridge from those intervals to global moment comparisons.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The representation neither locates zeros nor proves the stated moment asymptotics or the Riemann hypothesis. Moments also forget where large values and rapid variation occur, so extra endpoint inequalities and spacing assumptions are needed for gap conclusions.
directed.uncertainty: The displayed phase and exponents carry extraction risk, but the prose securely supports reality, modulus preservation, zero correspondence, and the distinct Z and Z' moment roles. The asymptotics are explicitly beliefs, not established facts here.

after.text:
Conrey et al. 4  established the moments of the derivative, on the unit circle, of
characteristic polynomials of random unitary matrices and used this to formulate a conjecture
for the moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta-function on the critical line. Their
method depends on the fact that the distribution of the eigenvalues of unitary matrices gives
insight into the distribution of zeros of the Riemann zeta-function and the values of the
characteristic polynomials of the unitary matrices give a model for the value distribution
of the Riemann zeta-function. Their formulae are expressed in terms of a determinant of a
matrix whose entries involve the I-Bessel function and, alternately, by a combinatorial sum.

This so-called pair correlation conjecture plays a complementary role to the Riemann
hypothesis. This conjecture implies the essential simplicity hypothesis that almost all zeros
of the zeta-function are simple. On the other hand, the integral on the right hand side is the
same as the one observed in the two-point correlation of the eigenvalues which are the energy
levels of the corresponding Hamiltonian which are usually not known with uncertainty. This
observation is due to Dyson and it restored some hope in an old idea of Hilbert and Polya
that the Riemann hypothesis follows from the existence of a self-adjoint Hermitian operator
whose spectrum of eigenvalues correspond to the set of nontrivial zeros of the zeta-function.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The historical sequence reveals two separable levers in the same gap machine: improve the available Z/Z' moments, or strengthen the endpoint inequality that converts them into spacing. A variational inequality can itself be compressed into an algebraic Jacobi-Schur problem, making optimization more tractable.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source reports a bound Λ≥2.3452 obtained from fourth and mixed moments, then Λ≥2.8915 from a generalized Wirtinger inequality derived variationally. It says a later treatment simplified the calculus and converted it to classical equations involving Jacobi-Schur functions, and records further bounds conditional on RMT-predicted mixed moments.
directed.conceptual_reading: The method is modular: global moment identities quantify amplitude and derivative cost, while a local coercive inequality turns a hypothetical interval-length cap into a constraint. Better information in either module sharpens the output without changing the whole architecture.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Variational optimization is re-represented as an algebraic equation problem involving Jacobi-Schur functions. Moment formulas bridge global integrals to constants, and the Wirtinger inequality bridges those constants back to zero-ended intervals and normalized gaps.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This comparative survey does not reproduce the proofs of the cited bounds. The later values depend on conjectural RMT moments, so they are not unconditional consequences of the inequality alone.
directed.uncertainty: Several integral coefficients require scan verification, and the final display labels two different values as Λ(5), making at least one extracted index unsafe to infer. The qualitative progression of methods is explicit.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Pair correlation, limsup/liminf normalized consecutive gaps, critical-line-only Lambda, and positive-proportion r-step gaps encode different spacing questions and require distinct interpretations.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source's equalities and comparisons involving all zeros versus critical-line zeros are RH-sensitive, and the positive-proportion route is only summarized from prior work.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Do not collapse zero-spacing observables

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Comparing a continuous global average with a discrete local average changes the conclusion from a single extremal limsup to a quantified family of r-step gaps occurring on a stated subset of zeros. The useful intermediate object is thus an averaged local window spanning r zeros, not merely one consecutive interval.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Under RH and the mixed-moment conjecture (1.9), the cited method compares continuous global and discrete local averages. For fixed positive integer r it gives a lower bound for γ_{n+r}−γ_n at an allowed threshold θ and states that the inequality holds for more than c(log T)^{-4k} proportion of zeros up to T, with computable c(k,θ,r).
directed.conceptual_reading: Global-to-local averaging retains frequency information that a limsup discards and naturally handles multi-zero windows. It therefore answers a different spacing question from the extremal Λ statistic.
directed.representation_or_bridge: A continuous integral average is matched against a discrete average localized at zero ordinates. That comparison bridges moment data to counts of r-step gaps satisfying a threshold.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is a cited alternative and is not used in the paper's main proofs. It is conditional on RH and the stated moment model; moreover the displayed fraction c(log T)^{-4k} decreases with T, so it should not be paraphrased as a fixed positive density.
directed.uncertainty: The OCR makes the exact θ threshold and some bracketing in (1.33) unsafe. The averaging mechanism, r-step target, conditional assumptions, and logarithmic proportion statement are recoverable.

related_synthesis_entries.title: Replacing the mixed-moment coefficient bottleneck

risk_spans.reason: Section transition and definition of the b_k input formula.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The paper keeps the Wirtinger-to-gap architecture but replaces the mixed-moment coefficient bottleneck with separately available ordinary- and derivative-moment constants b_k and c_k. This extends finite instantiation from k=7 to k=15 and yields the advertised 6.1392 limsup factor, without supplying an asymptotic route beyond the coefficient table.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: After citing earlier Λ(7) bounds, the source proposes combining Wirtinger-type inequalities with moments of Z and Z'. Using b_k and c_k, it claims explicit Λ(k) formulas and a conditional lower bound Λ(15)≥6.1392, compared with the earlier Λ(7) value 4.71474396.
directed.conceptual_reading: The advance is a problem reframing around available inputs: separate function and derivative moments replace unavailable higher mixed-moment coefficients while leaving the endpoint-inequality mechanism intact. The gain is finite reach, not a proof that the family continues indefinitely.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The coefficient pair b_k,c_k converts conjectural ordinary and derivative moment asymptotics into a ratio suitable for Wirtinger gap bounds. Tabulated constants then instantiate the abstract method through k=15.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The advertised conclusion remains conditional on RH and the moment predictions, and the source reports no c_k continuation beyond 15. A limsup lower bound establishes arbitrarily large normalized gaps along a subsequence; by itself it does not justify a fixed-frequency reading of the word 'often' used in the prose.
directed.uncertainty: The quoted decimal bounds are legible, but this introductory span does not contain their derivations. Their evidential status is therefore an advertised conditional result, not independently verified computation here.
